subject: State EDU: privacy addendum, FERPA & FedRAMP-adjacent questions
messages:
From: Linda Martinez <linda.martinez@stateedu.gov>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-02-10T09:12:00-05:00
Subject: Request: privacy addendum + FedRAMP-adjacent controls info

Hi Hannah,

Thanks for the discussion yesterday. To move this through our procurement review we need the following:

- A signed privacy addendum / DPA with SCCs (or equivalent) that covers processing of student records where applicable (FERPA).
- Confirmation whether Redwood can accept state data residency requirements (data at rest in the continental US).
- Any FedRAMP-adjacent documentation you have (a controls mapping or statements of compliance for cloud security controls) — we know you aren’t FedRAMP authorized, but we need to understand alignment.
- A redacted SOC 2 Type II report and completed CAIQ or SIG questionnaire if available.
- A DPIA or summary for processing of personal data for minors (if you have one).

We also have a couple of specific questions: what categories of student data you process (if any), whether you process any health information that may implicate HIPAA/FERPA overlap, and whether you’re open to a 24-hour incident notification SLA for state data.

Can you confirm what you can provide and an estimate for when we can get the artifacts? Our internal timeline is to got to our legal committee by 2/24.

Thanks,
Linda Martinez
Procurement Officer
State Department of Education
itc-procure@stateedu.gov

---
Note: attaching a sample state addendum template in a follow-up email for your reference (we will accept DocuSign).

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. I’ve looped in Marissa (Sales lead for SDOE) and Dev (Security/Infra contact).

What we can provide immediately:
- Draft Redwood DPA (attached) with SCCs incorporated where required. See "Redwood_DPA_2026-v1.pdf" (attachment stub).
- Redacted SOC 2 Type II (PII sections redacted) — will attach SOC2-TypeII-Redacted-2025.pdf.
- Completed CAIQ extract (CAIQ-Answers-Redwood-2026.xlsx).
- Current subprocessor list (Subprocessor_List_2026.csv).

On the Qs:
- Data categories: For standard EDU deployments we typically process user account info (name, email), class rosters and content (when the customer ingests student content into prompts), and usage metadata. We do not ingest health records by design unless specifically provisioned under a separate BAA/contract.
- FERPA: Redwood can accept FERPA-related contractual language in an addendum; customers remain responsible for determining FERPA applicability — we support reasonable technical and contractual controls.
- Data residency: we can commit to US continental region hosting for an additional configuration fee; we’ll note this in the DPA margin.
- Incident SLA: we can commit to 24-hour initial notification for confirmed incidents affecting SDOE data (subject to our standard incident response process).

Dev — could you confirm encryption at rest/in transit, KMS options, and whether we need to produce a short DPIA summary for minor data?

Next steps: I’ll upload the artifacts to the shared drive and send a DocuSign link for the addendum once legal confirms final language. Targeting to get everything to you by 2/18.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Head of Sales Operations
Redwood Inference

Linda / Hannah — adding a few practical notes from Sales/Customer side:

- Attached CAIQ export includes our current answers and notes for any "partial" control coverage. See CAIQ-Answers-Redwood-2026.xlsx.
- Subprocessors: we list core cloud infra providers and telemetry vendors in Subprocessor_List_2026.csv. We can consider a narrow approval list if SDOE requires it (will add negotiation point).

Subject: Re: Request: privacy addendum + FedRAMP-adjacent controls info

Thanks — this is helpful. A few clarifying items before we route to legal: 

1) Student data categories: is there a place in the CAIQ or DPA where you list processing categories (e.g., roster, grades, assessments, PII, special category)? If not, please add a short appendix.
2) DPIA: the short summary will be acceptable for initial review, but legal may ask for a fuller DPIA later.
3) Incident notification: we need an agreed process for "confirmed incidents" — does 24 hours include weekends? (we prefer 24 business hours)
4) Subprocessors: the state cannot approve open-ended subprocessor lists. Please confirm willingness to commit to a 30-day notice + option for limited approval for new subprocessors that will access SDOE data.
5) DocuSign: please send the DocuSign link once the DPA is final.

Also — do you have a controls mapping that maps your internal controls to NIST 800-53 or FedRAMP controls? If you don’t have a formal mapping, a matrix that shows equivalencies will work for our compliance reviewers.

Appreciate the responsiveness.

Regards,
Linda Martinez
Procurement Officer
State Department of Education
